:::{#def-surprisal}
#### Surprisal (**self-information**, **information content**)

<!-- no-graph: the surprisal of x depends on the distribution of X, so it has no single graph; rem-surprisal-rarity describes how it grows as the probability shrinks -->

The **surprisal** of a possible value $x$ of a [discrete random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) $X$
with $\P(X=x) > 0$ is

$$\Surprisalf{x} \eqdef -\log \P(X=x).$$

The surprisal is also called the **self-information** [@goodfellow2016deep, p. 73]
or the **information content** [@bishop2006prml, p. 49] of $x$.
With the natural logarithm, the surprisal is measured in [nats](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/entropy.html#def-nat),
and with base 2 in [bits](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/entropy.html#def-bit).
Evaluating $\Surprisalf{\cdot}$ at the [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $X$ itself gives the random variable $\Surprisalf{X}$, whose value is $\Surprisalf{x}$ when $X = x$.
The notation leaves the [probability mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) of $X$ implicit.

:::
